children: Lending to eurozone businesses halved in August, a sign that rising borrowing costs following the European Central Bank's decision to raise its key interest rate are hindering investment.
The ECB on Friday said that bank loans to businesses totaled 11 billion euros ($12.52 billion) during the month, down from 22 billion euros in July and 27 billion euros in June.

The central bank raised its key interest rate to 2.25% from 2% in June, responding to a pickup in the annual rate of inflation as the U.S.-Iran war pushed energy prices higher. Earlier this month, it raised its key interest rate to 2.5%.
The sharp decline in bank lending to businesses since May suggests the tightening in monetary policy is having some impact on economic activity, and particularly on investment.
